newsitem.title: IRAQ: Iraq sends oil contracts to U.N. for approval-paper.
newsitem.headline: Iraq sends oil contracts to U.N. for approval-paper.

text.p: Iraq has sent oil contracts signed with international companies to the United Nations for approval, a senior Iraqi oil official said in press remarks published on Sunday.

Saddam Zeban al-Hassan, head of Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO), also said Baghdad had renewed contracts with international oil firms during the first phase of the oil deal except for British, Japanese and Dutch companies.

Under the oil-for-food deal, which went into effect last December, Iraq is allowed to sell $2 billion worth of oil over six months to buy food and medicine for Iraqis, suffering from U.N. sanctions imposed for Baghdad's 1990 invasion of Kuwait.

"The contracts with international companies for the second six months (of the oil deal) are completely ready and several of them have already been faxed to the United Nations for approval," Hassan was quoted by the daily al-Qadissiya as saying.
Baghdad had submitted to the U.N. sanctions committee on Iraq an oil pricing formula which was approved by the committee on Friday allowing Baghdad to sign contracts with individual oil companies.

"The oil source declared that Iraq had accredited the same contracts which it had signed with large oil companies during the first six months of the oil-for-food deal (with the U.N.) for the second six months," the newspaper said.
The government newspaper al-Jumhouriya quoted Hassan as saying, "Iraq excluded a number of contracts with Japanese, British and Dutch companies...for the second six months".
The paper gave no explanation for excluding these firms.
Iraqi Oil Minister Amir Muhammad Rasheed said last week that oil exports were expected to start in mid-August.
